operator_io_quirks: Backtick-quoted DDL identifiers; table names mixed case (Addresses, Party_Forms); column names lowercase with typos (inidividual_phone, service_descriptio) - keep original spelling, quote with " in generated SQL.
All tables tiny (5-15 rows); no huge-table sampling needed, but read_schema must still handle max_rows_per_table path.

DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no fractional secs); ts_fuzzer dispatch = 'Date|Number(int elements)' - first element '2016-08-24 23:52:48' does NOT parse as int, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
Party_Services has NO primary key (pk=[]) and no unique constraint; booking_id is NOT NULL but not PK - sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK.
Composite PKs: Organization_Contact_Individuals(individual_id,organization_id), Party_Addresses(party_id,address_id), Party_Forms(party_id,form_id) - composite-PK members get max_l0=30.
FK customer_id -> Parties.party_id (column name differs from parent PK name); FK mapping must use pragma foreign_key_list, not name matching.
All FKs resolve to existing parents (parent_exists=true); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no cycles - process_order is a clean DAG.

NOT NULL columns: service_type_code, form_type_code, payment_method_code, address_type_code, form_status_code, all composite-PK members, all *_from/*_started/service_datetime - TS does not enforce NOT NULL, so some rows will fail insert and be skipped.
Declared VARCHAR(n) but storage class text everywhere; INTEGER PKs store integer - affinity matches, no storage/declared contradiction.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs - checked=False for all columns, so p=0-on-checked never triggers.
country has distinct=1 ('USA'), state_province_county distinct=13 of 15 - low-cardinality columns where TS String fuzzer will inject implausible fresh strings.
zip_postcode samples are 3-digit strings ('193','227') - int-like strings, so String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) neighbors.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on all DATETIME columns: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max parsed originals (~2016-04 to 2018-03); fresh dates uniform in that range, so date_contact_to > date_contact_from ties are NOT guaranteed - likely FP source for temporal-ordering queries.

String fuzzer on names/emails/phones/addresses: 20% fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() plus 50% contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop char) - destroys email/phone/zip format, drives FN on LIKE '%@%' or regex-ish predicates.

String fuzzer on low-cardinality enums (service_type_code, payment_method_code, form_status_code, address_type_code): 5 original samples + pool values, but fresh random strings appear w.p. p - breaks equality/IN filters on these codes (FN).

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: range [-10^4,10^4] (scale=4 default for bare INTEGER? actually int family scale from args, none -> scale=4), perturb +-1/+-2 - PKs become large/negative, so joins still work but range predicates on ids shift.

FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement - child rows may repeat parent values, so 1:N joins produce duplicate-heavy results; missing ties (parent has fewer distinct than child rows) is a known TS miss.

Composite-PK tables: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate (individual_id,organization_id) tuples, then drop_unique_duplicates - but FK draws happen before filtering for self-FK only; here no self-FK, so child FK values drawn from filtered parents, may leave orphan-ish combos that still insert.
Party_Services has no PK: no dedup, so duplicate (customer_id,service_id,service_datetime) rows possible - COUNT(*) queries get inflated, COUNT(DISTINCT) stable.

NOT NULL violations (fresh strings never NULL, but Number/String samplers can emit None? base drops None; Date can emit None?) - rows failing NOT NULL are silently skipped, shrinking tables below chosen size, so join cardinalities drift.
country='USA' constant: TS String fuzzer will emit random strings, so WHERE country='USA' returns 0 rows in many instances - classic FN.
date_formed on Organizations (5 rows) gets fresh dates in 2016-2017 range; queries filtering date_formed by year will mostly match but boundary years may miss.
No CHECK/UNIQUE beyond PK: drop_unique_duplicates only acts on PKs, so no extra row loss from unique columns.
